nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$, $t$ and $u$ with $u \ne s$, the out-neighbour list of $u$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$ equals the out-neighbour list of $u$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Erasing an edge leaves the other out-neighbour lists unchanged

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, the out-neighbour list of $s$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$ is the out-neighbour list of $s$ in $G$ with every occurrence of $t$ removed, the remaining entries kept in their original order.
nodes.title: Out-neighbours of the source after erasing an edge

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph on $V$ and let $s, m, t \in V$. If $G$ has a walk of length exactly $a$ from $s$ to $m$ and a walk of length exactly $b$ from $m$ to $t$, then $G$ has a walk of length exactly $a + b$ from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Concatenation of walks

nodes.summary: A directed adjacency graph on a type $V$ consists of a list of vertices that has no duplicates and contains every element of $V$ (so $V$ is finite), together with, for each vertex $v$, an ordered list of the out-neighbors of $v$, in which entries may repeat.
nodes.title: Directed adjacency graph

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$, $t$, $u$ and $v$, there is an edge from $u$ to $v$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$ if and only if there is an edge from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ and it is not the case that both $u = s$ and $v = t$.
nodes.title: Edges after erasing an edge

nodes.summary: Let $V$ have decidable equality and let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph on $V$. For all $s, t \in V$, the transpose of $G$ has an edge from $s$ to $t$ if and only if $G$ has an edge from $t$ to $s$.
nodes.title: Edges of the transpose graph

nodes.summary: For a directed adjacency graph $G$ on $V$ and vertices $s, t \in V$, there is an edge from $s$ to $t$ in $G$ when $t$ occurs in the adjacency list of $s$.
nodes.title: Edge of a directed adjacency graph

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, erasing the edge $s \to t$ from $G$ and then erasing it again gives, at every vertex, the same out-neighbour list as erasing it once.
nodes.title: Erasing an edge twice gives the same out-neighbour lists

nodes.summary: Given a directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, erasing the edge $s \to t$ gives the directed-adjacency graph with the same vertex enumeration as $G$ whose out-neighbour list at $s$ is the out-neighbour list of $s$ in $G$ with every occurrence of $t$ removed (the remaining entries keep their order), and whose out-neighbour list at every other vertex is the same as in $G$.
nodes.title: Erasing a directed edge

nodes.summary: For a type $V$ with decidable equality, a directed adjacency graph $G$ on $V$ and vertices $s, t \in V$, the Boolean edge test of $G$ at $(s, t)$ returns true if and only if $G$ has an edge from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: The Boolean edge test is correct

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, the Boolean edge lookup for $s \to t$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$ returns false.
nodes.title: The erased edge is absent

nodes.summary: For a type $V$ with decidable equality, a directed adjacency graph $G$ on $V$ and vertices $s, t \in V$, the edge test of $G$ at $(s, t)$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when $t$ occurs in the adjacency list of $s$.
nodes.title: Boolean edge test

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$, $t$, $u$ and $v$, if $v$ is reachable from $u$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$, then $v$ is reachable from $u$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Reachability after erasing an edge implies reachability in the original graph

nodes.summary: In a directed adjacency graph $G$, a vertex $t$ is reachable from a vertex $s$ if and only if there is a natural number $n$ such that $G$ has a walk of length exactly $n$ from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Reachability by walks

nodes.summary: In a directed adjacency graph $G$, a vertex $t$ is reachable from a vertex $s$ if and only if, in the unit-labelled labelled transition system of $G$, there is a finite list of labels along which $s$ reaches $t$ by a multistep transition.
nodes.title: Reachability in the associated transition system

nodes.summary: In a directed adjacency graph $G$, a vertex $t$ is reachable from a vertex $s$ if and only if $(s, t)$ lies in the reflexive-transitive closure of the edge relation of $G$.
nodes.title: Reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of the edge relation

nodes.summary: If two directed adjacency graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ on $V$ are semantically equivalent, then for all $s, t \in V$, $t$ is reachable from $s$ in $G_1$ if and only if $t$ is reachable from $s$ in $G_2$.
nodes.title: Semantically equivalent graphs have the same reachability

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph on a vertex type with decidable equality, and let $G^{\mathsf{T}}$ be its transpose. For all vertices $s$ and $t$, $t$ is reachable from $s$ in $G^{\mathsf{T}}$ if and only if $s$ is reachable from $t$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Reachability in the transpose graph

nodes.summary: For a directed adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, $t$ is reachable from $s$ when the pair $(s, t)$ lies in the reflexive-transitive closure of the edge relation of $G$: either $s = t$, or a finite sequence of edges of $G$ leads from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Reachability in a directed graph

nodes.summary: Every directed adjacency graph $G$ is semantically equivalent to itself.
nodes.title: Semantic equivalence of directed adjacency graphs is reflexive

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph on a vertex type with decidable equality. The transpose of the transpose of $G$ is semantically equivalent to $G$, that is, it has exactly the same edges as $G$.
nodes.title: Transposing twice gives a semantically equivalent graph

nodes.summary: Two directed adjacency graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ on the same vertex type are semantically equivalent when they have the same edges: for all vertices $s$ and $t$, $G_1$ has an edge from $s$ to $t$ if and only if $G_2$ does.
nodes.title: Semantic equivalence of directed adjacency graphs

nodes.summary: If a directed adjacency graph $G_1$ is semantically equivalent to a directed adjacency graph $G_2$, then $G_2$ is semantically equivalent to $G_1$.
nodes.title: Semantic equivalence of directed adjacency graphs is symmetric

nodes.summary: For a directed adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, $s$ is adjacent to $t$ in the digraph associated with $G$ if and only if $G$ has an edge from $s$ to $t$, that is, $t$ occurs in the adjacency list of $s$.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the associated digraph

nodes.summary: The digraph associated with a directed adjacency graph $G$ on a vertex type $V$ is the directed graph on $V$ in which $s$ is adjacent to $t$ exactly when $G$ has an edge from $s$ to $t$. It forgets the order of the adjacency lists and the multiplicity of their entries.
nodes.title: The digraph of a directed adjacency graph

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system of a directed adjacency graph $G$ has the vertices of $G$ as states and a single label, and it has a transition from $s$ to $t$ exactly when $G$ has an edge from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: The transition system of a directed adjacency graph

nodes.summary: If a directed adjacency graph $G_1$ is semantically equivalent to $G_2$, and $G_2$ is semantically equivalent to $G_3$, then $G_1$ is semantically equivalent to $G_3$.
nodes.title: Semantic equivalence of directed adjacency graphs is transitive

nodes.summary: For directed adjacency graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ on a vertex type with decidable equality, if $G_1$ and $G_2$ are semantically equivalent, then their transposes are semantically equivalent.
nodes.title: Transposition preserves semantic equivalence

nodes.summary: For a directed adjacency graph $G$ on a vertex type with decidable equality, the transpose of $G$ has the same vertex enumeration as $G$, and the adjacency list of a vertex $v$ consists of the vertices $u$ such that $v$ occurs in the adjacency list of $u$ in $G$, each listed once and in the order of the vertex enumeration.
nodes.title: Transpose of a directed adjacency graph

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$ has the same vertex enumeration as $G$: the same list of vertices, in the same order.
nodes.title: Erasing an edge keeps the vertex enumeration

nodes.summary: For every directed-adjacency graph $G$, vertices $s$, $t$, $u$ and $v$, and natural number $n$, if there is a walk of length $n$ from $u$ to $v$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by erasing the edge $s \to t$, then there is a walk of length $n$ from $u$ to $v$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Walks after erasing an edge are walks in the original graph

nodes.summary: If two directed adjacency graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ are semantically equivalent, then for every natural number $n$ and all vertices $s$ and $t$, there is a walk of length $n$ from $s$ to $t$ in $G_1$ if and only if there is a walk of length $n$ from $s$ to $t$ in $G_2$.
nodes.title: Semantically equivalent graphs have the same walks

nodes.summary: In a directed adjacency graph $G$, for every natural number $n$ and all vertices $s$ and $t$, there is a walk of length $n + 1$ from $s$ to $t$ if and only if there is a vertex $v$ such that $(s, v)$ is an edge of $G$ and there is a walk of length $n$ from $v$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Splitting off the first edge of a walk

nodes.summary: For a directed adjacency graph $G$ on a vertex type with decidable equality, every natural number $n$ and all vertices $s$ and $t$, there is a walk of length $n$ from $s$ to $t$ in the transpose of $G$ if and only if there is a walk of length $n$ from $t$ to $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Walks in the transpose are reversed walks

nodes.summary: In a directed adjacency graph, there is a walk of length $0$ from a vertex $s$ to a vertex $t$ if and only if $s = t$.
nodes.title: Walks of length zero

nodes.summary: For a directed adjacency graph $G$, a natural number $n$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, there is a walk of length $n$ from $s$ to $t$ in $G$ when there are vertices $v_0, \dots, v_n$ with $v_0 = s$ and $v_n = t$ such that $(v_i, v_{i+1})$ is an edge of $G$ for every $i < n$.
nodes.title: Walks of a given length

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
